The Police Inspector Sri. Halappa S. N., from the then Anti Corruption Bureau, (for short, the ACB)
Bengaluru City has charge sheeted the accused for the offence punishable under Section 7(a) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 (for short the 'PC Act') in Crime No.14/2021.

2. Allegations in brief are that, the Kodigehalli police have got registered the FIR in Crime No.46/2021 against CW1 Sri. Bharath Shetty (for short, the informant) for offences punishable under Sections 420, 504, 506 r/w Sec. 34 of the IPC.
The accused Sri. Dayananda Swamy was working as personal assistant to the DCP of North-East division of Bengaluru city.
He has assured and demanded a sum of Rs.10 lakhs from CW1 to prevent his arrest and to get file the B report in the said crime.

He had received Rs.5 lakhs in advance from CW1 out of the demanded amount through Acb vs G N Dayananda Swamy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150537514/
2 his friend on 05.04.2021.

sentences.text: Subsequently while demanding the balance amount of Rs.5 lakhs, this accused has also threatened to get registration of false cases against the informant at the Yalahanka New town police station in connection with the transaction pertaining to residential sites bearing No.8, 9 and 10 at Sy.No.16/01 of Chikkabommasandra village, Yalahanka taluk unless he pay Rs.50 lakhs.
Now, according to the 4 Spl. C.C.1947/2022 prosecution, the accused has committed the afore referred offence.
3. The accused was enlarged on bail at the pre- cognizance stage.
After getting registration of the case, the copies of charge sheet were furnished to him under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
The charge in respect of the offence punishable under Section 7(a) of the PC Act has been framed, read over and explained the same to the accused in the language known to him.
As he pleaded not guilty, the trial of the case has been fixed.
The accused has contested the case through his counsel.
4. To prove its allegations, the prosecution has examined 12 witnesses as Pw.1 to 12 and got marked documents as per Ex.P-1 to P-21 apart the incriminating metal seal vide M.O.1.
After closure of the prosecution evidence and getting compliance of Section 437(A), the statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. has been recorded and explained the same to the accused.
He denies the incriminating circumstances appearing against him in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses.

The accused has not adduced any evidence but got marked the document as per Ex.D1 in support of his defense that,
he is an innocent.
5.
Heard arguments from both side.

Point for consideration is :
1. Does the prosecution prove beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused being the public servant has committed the offence punishable U/sec. 7(a) of the PC Act?
7. The above point is answered in the negative for the following:
REASONS 8. Point No.1 :- The informant is PW3 - Sri. Bharath Shetty.

On his complaint at Ex.P8 dated 10.06.2021, PW9 - Sri. Pramod Kumar the Dy.S.P of the then ACB is seen to have got registered the FIR as per Ex.P15 against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 7(a) of the P.C Act.

The Police Inspector PW12 - Sri. S. R. Veerendra Prasad has did the major portion of the investigation and the officer of the same cadre, PW11- Sri. Halappa S. N deposed to have submitted the charge-sheet to the Court after obtaining the prosecution sanction order.
The allegations of the charge-sheet are as narrated in detail at para 2 above.
But, the allegations as such are denied by the accused as false and claims that, he is totally an innocent of the alleged offence.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that, the accused is a public servant as defined under Section 2(c) of the PC Act in the capacity of the Assistant Sub-Inspector.

He was attached to the Kodigenahalli Police Station but, was working as the 6 Spl. C.C.1947/2022 personal assistant in the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Bengaluru North-East Division on OOD basis by the time, when the alleged offence took place between 06.04.2021 to 08.06.2021.
Thus, the order from the competent authority to prosecute the public servant as contemplated under Section 19 of the PC Act is a matter of statutory requirement.
So far as the accused of this case is concerned, PW1 - Smt. Nisha James admittedly was the competent authority to accord the sanction.
She deposes to have issued the prosecution sanction order vide Ex.P1.
Its correctness and validity is not under the challenge.
Therefore, no discussion is a matter of necessity in this regard.

10. As per the evidence adduced by PW8 Sri. Jagadish K the then Inspector of Kodigenahalli Police Station and documents at Ex.P14 issued by him, the informant was one of the accused in crime No.46/2021.
Similarly, he was an accused in crime No.158/2021 of the Yalahanka New Town Police Station as per Ex.P13 issued by the concerned Police Inspector PW7 - Sri. R. Punith Kumar.

Now,
the allegation in specific facing by the accused is that :
He has assured and demanded a sum of Rs.10 lakhs from the informant to prevent his arrest and get file the B report in the crime No.46/2021 and 96/2021.
He had received Rs.5 lakhs in advance from CW1 through his friend PW4 - Sri. Dayananda Kumar on 06.04.2021.

Subsequently while demanding the balance amount of Rs.5 lakhs, this accused has also threatened to get 7 Spl. C.C.1947/2022 register the false cases by his influence at the Yalahanka New town police station against the informant, unless he pay Rs.50 lakhs.
Interestingly, the informant has turned hostile and denies the allegations against the accused.
He maintained the same stand, despite the cross- examination did by the the learned Public Prosecutor at length.
According to him, he was forced by the then Assistant Commissioner of Police, Yalahanka Sub - Division to lodge the complaint at Ex.P8 against the accused of this case.
11. PW4 - Sri. Dayananda Kumar the friend of the informant and PW6 Sri. Narendra Kumar M. were admittedly close to each other.
Both of them are the material witnesses for the prosecution to prove its allegations.
PW4 deposes as if the informant has requested him to pay Rs.10,00,000/- to the accused so as to get file the B reports in two cases against him.

According to PW4, as he had Rs.2,00,000/- only with him, claims to have borrowed a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- from PW6 and paid in all Rs.5,00,000/- to the accused on 05.04.2021 in his office at Sahakara Nagara.
In fact, this portion of his evidence is not supported either by the informant or PW6.

Rather, his evidence gets contradicted with his own statement at Ex.D1 dated 07.06.2024 admittedly given in the departmental enquiry initiated in respect of the same allegation against the accused as hereunder :

4 12.
This contradictory evidence exposes the dubious conduct of PW4 in deposing different stories conveniently for unknown reasons.
This indeed destroys the reliability of his evidence.

Moreover,
his unbelievable and divergent versions would not get any support or corroboration.

In the circumstance, I am inspired to rely on the verdict of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Crl. A.
No.20006/2014 in the case of State represented by the Lokayukta Police Vs. Mahiboob & Another to accept the defence contention that, PW4 is not a trustworthy witness to rely upon his evidence.

Whereas, PW6 admits that, in the year 2021 he paid Rs.3,00,000/- of himself and Rs.2,00,000/- of PW4 in all Rs.5,00,000/- to the accused as he had requested with an undertaking to repay it within a week.
According to this witness, the accused has repaid the said amount after 10 days.
But, never refers anything about the informant and the alleged bribe as deposed by the PW4.
Therefore, his evidence is nothing to do with the allegations made by the prosecution.

13. No doubt, the evidence of PW12 to the extent that, on 15.06.2021 he had seized some documents with a cash of Rs.50,000/- from the house of the accused under the panchanama at Ex.P2, the DVD marked at Ex.P7 in the 9 Spl. C.C.1947/2022 office of PW4 under the mahazar at Ex.P4 and the spot mahazar at Ex.P1 drawn at the place of an incident, is supported by the pancha witness PW2 - Sri.
Sathish H. C and others.
But, the evidence adduced by the informant stating that, he has produced the DVD at Ex.P7 along with his complaint at Ex.P8 before the ACB Police on 10.06.2021 goes to disprove the seizure of Ex.P7.

Very interesting is the opinion of the forensic expert i.e., PW10 - Sri.
V. S. Chaturmuka on the DVD in his report at Ex.P16 :
4 video files found were not original devices.
The visual therein were found recorded from another display.
Hence, the genunity could not been ascertained etc.
Inspires to believe that, Ex.P7 must have been created by the Police for the purpose of this case, rather than supporting the prosecution allegations.

14. The evaluation of the evidence adduced by the prosecution witnesses referred hereinbefore and the circumstances emanating from the factual discussion makes unambiguous that, the allegation of the prosecution against the accused is baseless.
In the situation, the evidence of the investigating officer PW12 assumes no weightage for the appreciation.

Even for the sake of arguments, if the so-called payment of Rs.5,00,000/- by PW4 or PW6 to the accused is believed to be true, it cannot be basis to constitute an offence under Section 7 of the PC Act.

In this context, I feel relevant and inspired to refer the 10 Spl. C.C.1947/2022 following authorities of the Hon'ble Apex Court so as to get import the valuable guidance and decide the issue effectively.

1. (2024) 10 SCC 489 in the case of Mir Mustafa Ali Hasmi Vs. The state of Andra Pradesh.
2. (2023) SCC Online SC 280 in the case of Neeraj Dutt Vs. State (Government of NCT, Delhi).

In both the authorities, it has been held and pointed out the following essential ingredients required to be satisfied for establishing the offence punishable under Section 7(a) of the P.C Act.
a.
The work of the complainant must be pending before the accused.

5 b.

sentences.text: There must be a demand by the accused from the complainant for the illegal gratification to do the official favour.
c. There must be an acceptance and gratification amount in pursuance of such demand.
15. In fact, the prosecution is not disputing that, no work of any kind pertaining to the informant herein was pending before the accused to do the official favour.

The cross-examination admission of the investigating officer (PW12) at para 19 that,

Thus, needless to say that, the evidence of the prosecution itself goes to indicate its failure to prove the work pendency of any kind before the accused either on the date of the alleged offence or the date of complaint.

Therefore, I am to accept the defence contention that,
the alleged demand for the illegal gratification and its subsequent acceptance of Rs.5,00,000/- in advance from PW4 by the accused is an invented allegation being made for the purpose of this case.
Even, the informant is not disputing the evidence of PW6 that, at the request of the accused, he lent Rs.5,00,000/- in the form of hand loan and got it repaid within 10 days.

Therefore, neither this amount nor the amount of Rs.50,000/- cash admittedly seized under the mahazar at Ex.P2 dated 15.06.2021 from the house of the accused, be connected to the charge-sheet allegations in any manner.

In the light of the above, needless to indicate the prosecution's failure to constitute the essential ingredients of the offence under Section 7 of P.C Act against the accused and bring home his guilt beyond all reasonable doubt.
In other words, this is a clear case of an acquittal.

Accordingly,
I pass the following :

ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973, the accused Sri. Dayananda Swamy is acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 7(a) of The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
His bail bonds shall stand cancelled forthwith.
The metal seal at MO1 shall be returned to the jurisdictional police after appeal period is over.

The cash of Rs.50,000/- seized from the house of the accused under the mahazar at Ex.P2 dated 15.06.2021 is ordered to return to the accused on proper identification and as per the procedure, if not already returned.
(Dictated to the Steno Gr.3 directly on computer, computerized by him, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the open Court on this the 04 th day of September, 2025).
Sd/- 04.09.2025 (K.M. RADHAKRISHNA) XXIII Addl.
